note: Re-judged 2026-11-12 after runSession changed to take onDone func(operational bool): a local operational is set true in the on-operational callback just before SessionUp is published, and the first defer became func() { onDone(operational) }(). The defer order (kaCancel, panic guard, Stop, onDone) is unchanged, and the KeepAlive sender goroutine (waits on accepted, re-reads currentKeepalive()/3 each cycle, re-arms on KeepaliveChanged, SendKeepalive on each tick), the accepting KeepAlive in the on-init callback, and handleInit's negotiation are byte-identical, so ze's KeepAlive behaviour and the judgement below stand; both tagged units are unchanged (only the runSessionForTest helper's onDone literal took the new signature). RFC 5036 Section 3.5.4.1: "An LSR MUST arrange that its peer receive an LDP message from it at least every KeepAlive Time period." Re-judged 2026-10-28 after d9fa580dce added the panic-guard defer, which acts only on a recovered panic. Re-judged 2026-10-14 after TestRFC5036KeepalivesSentPeriodically changed. Positive: runSession to operational with both sides at 1s and an empty LIB; each of the next three PDUs must be a KeepAlive and each gap at most 1s; the test peer writes a KeepAlive after each one so ze's 1s KeepAlive Timer is fed, which removes no assertion. Negative (dual-tagged with RFC5036-3.5.4.1-1): TestRFC5036KeepalivePacingFollowsNegotiatedTime has ze propose 60s and the peer 1s, then requires each of the next three PDUs within 1s of the previous; it does not check their type, which the row allows (any LDP message will do), and a sender pacing from the 60s proposal fails it because the session ends after the 1s timer and the next read fails. Row-quality: the first sentence duplicates RFC5036-3.5.4.1-1 verbatim.
